stories.headline: Don't be surprised if Jordan Love makes history and Mendoza performs like a QB1
stories.summary: Elite WRs compensate for the lack of a run game in Green Bay, while there's unwarranted caution for Vegas' QB.
stories.body:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!

NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.

Don't be surprised if ... Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love becomes the 10th to pass for 5,000 yards in a season

MVP candidate Love continues to shine, throwing for 372 yards in Sunday's high-scoring road victory over the New England Patriots. With eight games left in the regular season, Love boasts a league-leading 2,618 passing yards, pacing toward 4,945 yards. Nine quarterbacks in NFL history have thrown for 5,000 yards, doing so 15 times. Matthew Stafford, Justin Herbert, Patrick Mahomes (twice) and -- of course -- Jameis Winston are the only active QBs to have done so.

The Packers cannot run the football effectively, forcing Love to throw more than the team's original plan. Love threw for 4,159 yards in his first season as starter back in 2023 but had 11 interceptions, and the team went 9-8. They wanted Love to take fewer chances, release the ball quicker and play more efficiently. Last season, the Packers went 9-5-1 in Love's 15 starts, as he threw for only 3,381 yards with a mere six interceptions. The Packers were fifth in the league in rushing in 2024 and 15th in 2025. That plan worked, and it figured to be the plan again.

Let's just say things haven't worked out in the running game -- thanks to offensive line and running back issues -- and there is little indication that will change in the coming weeks and months. The Packers are last in the NFL with 68.2 rushing yards per game. (For perspective, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers average 163.9.) The Packers average a brutal 3.0 yards per carry because healthy, proven options are limited. Love must throw often for the team to succeed and he has a pair of top-10 WRs in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The Packers are 6-3, in last place in a tough division, but their path to January is Love piling on numbers.

Sticking with the powerful NFC North, it sure would be anything but bold to predict Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson will return to WR1 status now that the franchise reunited with a competent QB in Kirk Cousins. Watching Carson Wentz against the Buffalo Bills on Monday was painful, regardless of rooting interest and Jefferson looked miserable. Now he won't be! What if this division now boasts more than half of the top 10 WRs in fantasy this season? Assume the two Packers, plus Jefferson, Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown and ... has anyone noticed Chicago Bears WR Luther Burden III is currently No. 10? Inconsistent but tantalizing Lion Jameson Williams is 19th in WR scoring, but capable of delivering 20-point outings at any time. How about six of the top 10 WRs in one division? Perhaps!

Don't be surprised if ... Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza performs like a deep-league QB1 option

I suppose one could reasonably debate whether the Raiders did the right thing in moving Cousins to the Vikings because it means the team must turn to Mendoza, the top pick in the NFL draft, potentially before he is ready. Then again, how do you find out if a QB is ready? Watch Mendoza step right in and perform much the way Cousins was doing, rocking the play-action pass and leaning heavily on TE Brock Bowers and RB Ashton Jeanty (as a receiver). Perhaps the Raiders will barely adjust a gameplan that is working. The Raiders are eighth in points this season. They don't think Mendoza will fail. Why should we?

Fantasy managers should be aggressive in adding Mendoza, though not necessarily activating him this week against a Seattle Seahawks defense that stymied Kansas City Chiefs QB Mahomes in Week 7. Then again, the Seahawks permitted 30 points in three games this season, to QBs Caleb Williams, Brock Purdy and ... Marcus Mariota! The Seahawks haven't seen Mendoza before. Again, I am not saying he scores 20 fantasy points or the Raiders score 20 points, but let's not be so dismissive. Perhaps the Raiders will even win the game at home.

After Seattle, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos, who rank 19th in permitting QB fantasy points this season. They're not No. 2, like the Seahawks. The Broncos get thrown on and they are permitting 355 yards per game, fourth in the NFL. It's a common mistake in evaluating fantasy options for managers to simply assume because everyone told them the Broncos were formidable. The Raiders also face the Los Angeles Chargers, Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans before the end of the season.

Only the Packers rank worse in rushing yards per game. The Raiders must throw the football, and Mendoza is certainly capable of making the same throws that Cousins was thriving at. Also, who are the QBs outside the top 10 in season scoring that may be starters for deep-league fantasy managers? Bryce Young, Tyler Shough, Stafford, Bo Nix? Why can't Mendoza be comparable for fantasy scoring? OK, don't expect Cousins-type numbers for the rookie, but I don't think we will be ranking Mendoza so cautiously after this week.

Another Raiders thought: Jeanty may not be the RB1 option so many fantasy managers expected, but he isn't a fantasy bust. He is 14th in running back scoring because he leads the position in receptions and he boasts more receiving yards than rushing ones. That is not entirely his fault as the Raiders struggle to run block. Jeanty is an electric option as a receiver, averaging 8.8 yards per catch, which is excellent for a running back. No top 30 RB had more receiving yards than they did rushing yards last season, though Kenny Gainwell came relatively close as a Pittsburgh Steeler. Jeanty may do so.

Don't be surprised if ... San Francisco 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey fails to rush for 1,000 yards

This isn't the first time we have discussed McCaffrey and his lack of volume this year, but really, this is all working out quite well for fantasy managers. Only three running backs boast more fantasy points than McCaffrey, even though he's tied for 22nd in rushing attempts (with Rhamondre Stevenson and Omarion Hampton). Oh, so you think McCaffrey must have a million receptions, right? Nope, his 36 catches are tied with Kyren Williams for third among RBs, but this is hardly a pace for 102 receptions, like last season. It is a pace for 76 catches.

Credit the 49ers for keeping the mercurial McCaffrey productive and healthy. Many were skeptical. He totaled a ridiculous 413 touches last season. Everyone expected some regression, but now he is pacing toward a manageable 292 touches. That is a huge dropoff and, while acknowledging McCaffrey has gone from averaging 24.5 fantasy points per game to 20.8 points is a big deal, we certainly cannot complain! McCaffrey has 10 touchdowns. He hasn't missed a game. He remains a fantasy star despite pacing for just 971 rushing yards.

Still, backup 49er Kaelon Black remains available in 65% of ESPN standard leagues. I think he should be more popular for the final months, not only if one rosters McCaffrey, but just in general. If McCaffrey were to get hurt (and nobody is rooting for this), this would be a potential RB1 option. Of course, we may say this about myriad RBs available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues, right? Or would we?

Kansas City Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson looks like a future star and the Chiefs are trying harder to get the football to this fellow in open space, where he is dynamic. Nobody wants Kenneth Walker III to get injured either, but Johnson could be a legit RB1 if he gets a chance. The Chiefs and 49ers are built and managed well. Their backup RBs could be special. Would Seth McGowan rock if the Indianapolis Colts had traded the great Jonathan Taylor? Perhaps, but it is not the same as Black and Johnson. Khalil Herbert in Atlanta? C'mon. Justice Hill with the Ravens? Detroit's Sione Vaki? No, Black and Johnson stand out to me.

stories.headline: Who has won the MLB MVP Award? All-time winners list
stories.summary: MLB's MVP Award is given to top players in the American League and National League. Take a look at the all-time winners list now.
stories.body:
There are two MVPs in Major League Baseball each year -- one in the American League and one in the National League. Since 1931, the Baseball Writers' Association of America has voted for the MVPs at the end of the regular season and before the start of the postseason.

The award began in 1911 as the Chalmers Award, honoring the "most important and useful player to the club and to the league." That award was discontinued in 1914. From 1922 to 1928 in the AL and from 1924 to 1929 in the NL, the League Award was presented to "the baseball player who is of the greatest all-around service to his club." Prior winners were not eligible to win the award again during that time.

In 2026, Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros won MVP for the American League, the 3rd Astros player to win the award after Jose Altuve in 2017 and Jeff Bagwell in 1994. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs won for the National League, the first Cubs player to win it since Kris Bryant in 2016.

Florida Panthers (11-7-2, in the Atlantic Division) vs. St. Louis Blues (9-8-2, in the Central Division)


St. Louis; Saturday, 7 p.m. EST


BOTTOM LINE: The Florida Panthers visit the St. Louis Blues after Anton Lundell scored two goals in the Panthers' 5-4 win against the Detroit Red Wings.


St. Louis is 9-8-2 overall and 5-2-1 in home games. The Blues have a 7-1-1 record in games they score at least three goals.


Florida has a 6-5-2 record in road games and an 11-7-2 record overall. The Panthers lead league play with 111 total penalties (averaging 5.6 per game).

stories.headline: Messi up for record 3rd MLS MVP award; Sullivan, 17, gets historic nomination
stories.summary: Lionel Messi has been named a finalist for the 2026 MLS MVP award, as he seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi has been named a finalist for the 2026 Major League Soccer MVP award, as the Inter Miami captain seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.

Messi won the MVP award in 2024 and 2025, becoming the second player to ever win the trophy twice, alongside Preki (Predrag Radosavljević), who won the title in 1997 and 2003.

- Will MLS teams' regular-season momentum last the two weeks before the playoffs start?

- Every eliminated MLS team: What worked and what didn't in 2026, what needs improving in 2027?

- Brotherly love: Cavan, Quinn Sullivan both score as Philly soars into playoffs

Eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Messi already clinched a record second straight Golden Boot award after scoring 26 goals in the 2026 regular season.

Messi joins finalists Evander (FC Cincinnati), Guilherme (Houston Dynamo FC) Hany Mukhtar (Nashville SC), and Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union) for the award, which is named after former U.S. men's national team great Landon Donovan.

At 17 years old, Sullivan stands as the youngest player in MLS history to be named a finalist for the MVP award. He is also a finalist for the MLS Young Player of the Year award.

Last month, Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history when he found the net against Mexico.

MVP candidate Guilherme was named a finalist for the MLS Newcomer of the Year award, alongside Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City SC). Guilherme recorded 16 goals and 10 assists, while Griezmann managed 14 goals and eight assists.

Griezmann earns the recognition after joining Orlando City in July after finishing the 2025-26 season with Atlético Madrid in Spain.

Finalists for each end-of-the-year award received the highest average in votes from MLS club technical staff, MLS first-team players and select media members. Each group accounted for 33.3% of the overall results, according to MLS.

Winners will be announced during the 2026 playoffs, which begin on Nov. 19.

stories.headline: UFC's Josh Hokit says he'll 'never' regret vulgar Michelle Obama remarks
stories.summary: UFC fighter Josh Hokit, who will challenger for the heavyweight title on Saturday, says he'll "never" regret his vulgar comments about former First Lady Michelle Obama,
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit said he has no regrets about using the White House as a bully pulpit to make an extraordinary and unfounded attack based on a right-wing conspiracy theory about former first lady Michelle Obama.

Hokit made his vulgar remarks inside the Octagon in June after winning his fight at the UFC event to mark President Donald Trump's 80th birthday on the South Lawn of the White House.

Hokit fights for the first time since then on Saturday when he challenges heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.

Hokit again made a series of crass insults about other fighters on the fight card on Wednesday inside a New York hotel before taking questions about his championship bout and his remarks on Obama.

"I'll never look back and be like, I regret that," Hokit said.

Wearing a black stocking cap over an American flag bandana, sunglasses and fight gloves, Hokit said he "took the rap of a villain" before he burst into what he called a freestyle rap to express his lack of regret.

Hokit said he was "sure it wasn't" the right thing to do to insult the former first lady but was proud the remarks had put his image on Trump's Truth Social posts. In one post, Hokit appeared in cartoon form alongside UFC chief Dana White in the White House briefing room.

Trump said over the weekend he had offered White the job of White House press secretary. White declined the frivolous offer.

"I'm here to take what's mine," Hokit said. "If I've got to rub some people the wrong way, if I've got to say some (stuff) in the wrong location, it is what it is. Was it not a good location to say it? I mean, we're at the White House. That house represents freedom of speech. So it is what it is. I think it was the perfect location to say it."

The 28-year-old Hokit is 10-0 in his MMA career and has won all six fights since joining UFC in 2025.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to let aid trucks into Gaza after visiting the Rafah border this week, adding in a passionate post "the past three years of Israel's genocide is appalling."
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to let aid trucks into Gaza after visiting the Rafah border this week, adding in a passionate post "the past three years of Israel's genocide is appalling."

The seven-time world champion called for a "Free Palestine" during a news conference ahead of October's United States Grand Prix, and has previously called for a ceasefire in the region.

This week, Hamilton visited the Rafah crossing, the only land crossing between the Gaza Strip and Egypt and the hub of various humanitarian aid organizations.

After meeting aid workers and truck drivers on the ground, Hamilton posted a message about the trip to his 44 million Instagram followers.

"The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling," Hamilton wrote on Instagram. "It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less."

Israel denies accusations of genocide, saying its military campaign in Gaza targets militants of terrorist group Hamas. Hamilton urged people not to ignore what is happening in the region.

"I know so many people that feel that same helplessness," he added. "That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

- Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale

Hamilton also met with North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer.

The governor's office shared videos to its official Facebook page of Hamilton being briefed by Megawer on the aid coordination and the Ferrari driver greeting aid workers and inquiring how often they were able to enter Gaza through the Rafah crossing.

Last month, the World Health Organization (WHO) said repeated delays in bringing life-saving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies into Gaza can have "devastating consequences" for Palestinians who urgently need them.

Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go in, only to be delayed or not allowed in.

His post continued: "I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.

"At the Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours. At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.

"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse."

stories.body:

State of play and players to know
Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Murray, Gayfer, Wil Malady and Leo Steed have also received invites in a sign of club interest on night one.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.

stories.headline: How the Atlanta Dream turned their franchise around in just five years
stories.summary: Five years ago, the Dream were the second-worst team in the WNBA -- making their Finals run all the more remarkable.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Just five years ago, the idea of the Atlanta Dream competing for the WNBA championship trophy would have seemed as unlikely as a rebound landing untouched next to Angel Reese.

So finishing within one victory of a title, as the Dream did in the WNBA Finals last week, says a lot about just how far the franchise has come since 2021. Even without the 2026 championship, what the Dream did in revitalizing their franchise is a story that shouldn't be lost in Golden State's celebration. Five years ago, the Dream were a mess. Now, they're contenders. That's something other WNBA franchises can look to.

"It's remarkable, really," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said.

Consider how far the franchise was from this in 2021.

That was the year the Dream moved to Gateway Center Arena -- the smallest venue in the WNBA at 3,500 seats -- because too much of their longtime larger home (State Farm Arena, capacity 17,608) was vacant during games. The Dream had three different coaches that year, one resigning just before the season began to take a college job. Chennedy Carter, their lottery-pick selection from 2020, was suspended in July and never returned. They finished in second-to-last place in the WNBA at 8-24.

The team's most notable moment came not on court, but in a viral video of two Dream players throwing punches by a food truck outside an Atlanta nightclub.

Those were the low points. But behind the scenes, two big moves in 2021 helped spark a turnaround: an ownership change, led by real estate investor Larry Gottesdiener, and a new general manager, Dan Padover.

Reese was then a college sophomore with huge goals for her future. But it wasn't until this April that she knew those plans would intersect with the Dream.

"When I play with joy and I'm surrounded by people that just genuinely make me happy, I think I'm at my best," Reese said. "The organization has poured into me. To be in my third year [in the WNBA], this is obviously the best situation I've ever been in."

And even as Reese and teammates Jordin Canada and Allisha Gray sat somberly in the Dream's postgame news conference after Game 7, the joyful sounds of Ballhalla's celebration audible, they looked dissatisfied but not devastated.

"They changed my life," Reese said of the Atlanta players and staff. "And I'm just so grateful for them."

A 2008 EXPANSION TEAM, the Dream's first title hopes were led by another Angel -- 2009 No. 1 pick Angel McCoughtry. She led the Dream to the Finals in 2010, 2011 and 2013, but they were swept each time.

The Dream then missed the playoffs six of the next nine years. They won a then-franchise record 23 games in 2018, but lost McCoughtry to a knee injury Aug. 7 and lost 3-2 in the semifinals.

Without McCoughtry in 2019, the Dream averaged just 4,270 fans for home games, necessitating the move from State Farm Arena. That relocation was delayed a year because of the COVID-19 pandemic, when the 2020 season was in a "bubble" in Bradenton, Florida. By then, McCoughtry had left in free agency for Las Vegas.

The Dream's leadership became a focus for all WNBA players in the bubble when co-owner Kelly Loeffler sent a letter to commissioner Cathy Engelbert opposing the league's decision to display "Black Lives Matter" logos on the courts in Bradenton. Loeffler wrote "we need less -- not more -- politics in sports."

Loeffler was involved in a political race at the time, seeking to hold her U.S. Senate seat. The divide mushroomed into WNBA players campaigning for her opponent, Raphael Warnock.

"Being on the outside of the Dream looking in then, during that time everybody was rallying around them," said guard Jordin Canada, then with the Seattle Storm, of the bubble activism against Loeffler's continued ownership. "We wanted what was best for them and the W as a whole, and to see that transition into a more positive direction."

The situation was untenable, and the franchise was sold in February 2021 to Gottesdiener's group, which included former WNBA player Renee Montgomery.

"I believed the WNBA was an extraordinary opportunity, not just to grow the game of basketball," Gottesdiener said, "but to demonstrate what's possible when you invest in women."

Padover, who joined the Dream in October 2021, had worked for the Las Vegas Aces for three years, helping build the team that would become a three-time champion. He went from a franchise a step from the top to one with nowhere to go but up.

Padover started his WNBA career as a video coordinator with the New York Liberty in 2012, and he has credited former coach and GM Bill Laimbeer for helping him develop into a team executive. He cites this key from Laimbeer.

"If you can get your organization organized and you can take care of the players, you can start to establish yourself as a place that is respected," Padover said. "Under previous ownership, I think we were disorganized, and we didn't really have an identity.

"When I got here the goal was, 'Let's turn Atlanta back into a franchise that's respected throughout the WNBA community, one piece at a time, and that will allow us to be able to build something.' We started with things like player housing, staffing, and medical and player development."

THE OTHER PIECE was putting the right players and coaches in the building. Padover, who has been named the league's executive of the year three times, put his trade wizardry to use. He dealt the Nos. 3 and 14 picks in the 2022 draft and a 2023 pick swap to Washington for the No. 1 pick in 2022 to select Rhyne Howard.

"It was a huge boost of confidence," Howard said. "Obviously, when you get drafted, that means the team wants you. But to do it in the way that they did -- trading up to get me like that -- put no doubt in my mind that I was a piece that they were looking for to start this new journey, to start this new outcome that we're having."

The 6-foot-2 guard was Rookie of the Year and has since been a four-time All-Star. She averaged 17.7 points in the regular season this year and 16.3 in the playoffs. Howard won't recall Game 7 fondly -- she was limited to six points on 3-of-14 shooting -- but she took noticeable steps forward as a player in 2026, especially on defense.

Padover also got the steal of the second round in 2022 with forward Naz Hillmon, who became a full-time starter this season and has played more WNBA games than anyone from that draft class.

Subsequent huge deals came for guards Gray (2023) and Canada (2024).

"One of the things that I definitely took from Bill was not to be skittish to give up things in trades," Padover said. "If you're doing it to get a great player, it's always worth it, and don't be afraid to do that."

One of Padover's biggest moves in 2025 was bringing in Smesko, who had spent most of his career as a college coach, including 17 years at Florida Gulf Coast.

"Obviously, there was a changing landscape in college basketball, and I was at the point where a new challenge was needed," Smesko said of his decision to move to the WNBA. "It was Atlanta, and I love the city. And I thought there was the makings of a core that could compete for a championship."

Atlanta went 30-14 last season but lost in the first round of the playoffs. Padover used a trade to acquire the last key component. On April 6, the Dream obtained Reese from the Chicago Sky for future draft picks. Reese had become disillusioned with the Sky's direction and voiced her concerns near the end of the 2025 season. She believed in the Dream's vision, just as the players obtained before her did.

"I feel like the organization has gotten to a point where players want to come play for Atlanta," Gray said. "To be able to get Angel just speaks volumes of how the organization is run and how it really cares for players. The city of Atlanta is great. Great culture. The games just feel like one big family cookout, and everybody's welcome."

Reese proved to be the final and most essential ingredient. Other than a five-game skid June 24-July 4, the Dream -- who also added veteran DeWanna Bonner late in the season -- stayed consistent, finishing 30-14 again. Reese had the best offensive year of her career, averaging 16.4 points, plus 12.1 rebounds.

"She's made me look good all season long," Howard said. "And I'm sure she's going to continue to do that for the rest of her time here. Shoutout to her for coming in and being bought in. She's handled every challenge that we've thrown at her with grace."

This year's Finals games in Atlanta didn't come without hurdles -- facility conflicts with State Farm Arena meant one Finals game had to be moved up a day and another had to be played at 12:30 p.m. ET on a Thursday. But even that early game was joyful and loud, a full house of fans skipping work and school to cheer on the Dream in a must-win Game 6.

Next year, the Dream moves back to State Farm Arena full time, playing all 25 regular-season home games there.

And as disappointed as the Dream were after losing Game 7, they also immediately expressed excitement about the 2027 season.

"Just because we didn't win today doesn't mean that we won't be champions in the future," Reese said.

Those words weren't just platitudes after a disappointing ending. Next year, with every starter already signed to return, the Dream could at last win that elusive title.

"I like our chemistry and just the sisterhood that we have as a team," said Gray, who played every Finals game despite sustaining an injury on her shooting hand in the semifinals. "We actually love each other and enjoy being around each other."

stories.headline: Subtle reason Jillaroo will cause Cup final headaches
stories.summary: Jillaroos fullback Tamika Upton has explained why Jesse Southwell commanded selection for the World Cup final against New Zealand.
stories.body:
The numbers are impressive, but it's what doesn't show up on the stats sheet that Tamika Upton likes most about Jesse Southwell.

The Brisbane five-eighth won a tight selection battle to replace Sydney Roosters premiership winner Jocelyn Kelleher for Sunday's Women's World Cup final.

Kelleher started in three of Australia's four Cup games and was player of the match in the 40-0 win over Samoa on Test debut.

Southwell, who will partner Tarryn Aiken in the halves, filled her boots with 44 points of her own in the record-breaking 124-6 win over Wales.

Kelleher kicks goals too and shared a strong bond with Roosters teammate and halfback Aiken during their NRLW title win, but has been named in the 21 jersey for the clash with New Zealand.

"Tarryn and Jesse haven't played too much footy together, but I've been fortunate to play a lot with the both of them and watching them both link up is going to be pretty special," Australia and Brisbane fullback Upton said.

"The best thing about Jesse, and this goes unnoticed and without stats, is how much space she creates for the people outside of her.

"I've been fortunate enough to have that pretty much my whole career, and I'm excited for her to do that for Taryn and make her job a little bit easier.

"She's young, she's energetic, she's enthusiastic, she wants the ball and she wants to be a part of the game."

Australia cruised into the final four before receiving a welcome test in their comeback semi-final defeat of Fiji.

"The record-breaking games are probably not the best when you're prepping for finals footy, which is so different," Upton said.

"We've had the luxury of everything working out for us and that just doesn't happen when it comes to finals.

"So it was good to be under the pump."
